content: {"summary":"The incident was caused by connection‑pool exhaustion on two orders‑api pods due to long‑running queries, while the database had ample connection slots.","likely_cause":"Connections were exhausted on orders‑api‑02 and orders‑api‑03 because slow queries kept them checked out, not because the database ran out of slots.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"At 10:15 the pools on two orders‑api pods hit their 25‑connection ceiling, leading to request failures.","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#1"],"quote":"Pool usage on the two pods rose to its ceiling of 25 first."},{"text":"The orders‑db had sufficient capacity (300 connections) so the shortage was not at the database level.","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#1"],"quote":"orders-db allows 300 connections, while orders‑api runs three pods"},{"text":"The root issue was long‑running queries holding connections, not the total number of connections available.","evidence_ids":["INC-0182#1"],"quote":"The trouble sat in how long each connection was held, not in how many could be opened."}],"next_checks":["Identify the slow query that kept connections occupied","Add a gauge to monitor pool usage per pod ahead of the ceiling","Review pool timeout and max‑connection settings for orders‑api","Check if similar pool‑exhaustion patterns appear in later logs"]}
